summary: Charles Norman Seddon was an Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford (1889–1891) and was Reader in Persian and Marathi at the University of Oxford from 1924.
Charles Oman was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at New College, Oxford (circa 1878–1882) and subsequently held a post at the University of Oxford from circa 1883 to 1946.

Charles Otto Blagden was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. Educated at Dulwich College and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (circa 1882–1886), he later held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 1917 to 1935.

Indologist and linguist Charles Philip Brown studied at East India Company College and under traditional teachers Kodandarama Panthulu, Tippabhatla, and Vatthyam. He served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1817–1854) and was Professor of Telugu at UCL (circa 1865–1879).
Charles Picard was a historian and archaeologist. He held academic appointments at the University of Lyon from circa 1919 to 1934 and at the University of Paris from circa 1934 to 1955.

Charles Ramble works in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Durham University and Oxford under Michael Aris, he held posts at Oxford (2002–2005) and became Director of Studies at École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2009.

Charles Rieu studied at Geneva and Bonn under Lassen, Freytag, Gildemeister, and Humbert. A scholar of Indology, Iranian studies, and linguistics, he held posts at the British Museum, UCL (1856–1894), and Cambridge (1895).

Charles Robert Wilson worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at City of London School, Wadham College, and Oxford, later serving in the Bengal Education Department (1887) and as Principal of Patna College (circa 1900–1902).

Indologist and linguist Charles Rockwell Lanman studied at Yale and in Germany under Whitney, Hadley, Weber, Roth, Curtius, and Leskien. He taught at Johns Hopkins (1876–1880) and served as Professor at Harvard University from 1880 to 1926.

Charles S. Prebish is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Case Western Reserve under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson, later serving as Professor of Religious Studies at Pennsylvania State University (circa 1972–2007).

Charles Schoebel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and under Eugène Burnouf. In 1845, he worked as a schoolteacher of German at Lycée de Reims and Collège Sainte-Barbe.
Charles Swynnerton was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. He was educated at University College London and the University of Oxford, and he served as Headmaster of Ramsey Grammar School.

Charles Taliaferro is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College, University of Rhode Island, Harvard Divinity School, and Brown University, and served as a professor at St. Olaf College from circa 1985 to 2022.

Charles Taylor is a philosopher who was educated at Selwyn House School, McGill University, and Balliol College, Oxford. He served as Professor of Political Science at McGill (circa 1961–1998) and held a post at Northwestern University (circa 2002–2011).

Charles Ulysse Renel was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École Normale Supérieure, and Lyon under Paul Regnaud. He held posts at Caen (1897), Franche-Comté (1898), and the University of Lyon (1900).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at National Taiwan University (circa 1952–1960) and the University of Illinois System (circa 1965–1969), and later held a post at Ohio University (circa 1968–1972).

Indologist and linguist Charles Wilkins studied under Kālinātha and co-founded The Asiatic Society in 1784. He held librarian positions with the East India Company and the India Office Library from circa 1800 until 1836.

Charles Willemen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied under William Reynolds Beal Acker. He held an appointment as a professor at Ghent University, attested between 1999 and 2001.

Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin worked in Iranian studies, sinology, and Indology. He studied law at the University of Liège, directed Collège Saint-Quirin, and was Professor of Sanskrit at KU Leuven / Université catholique de Louvain from 1871.

Charlotte Krause was an Indologist who studied at Tübingen, Berlin, Marburg, Leipzig, and under Garbe, Windisch, Hertel, and Vijaya Indra Suri. She was Hertel’s assistant at Leipzig (circa 1920–1923) and Curator at Scindia Oriental Institute (1942–1947).
